keyFindings.description: The process backend's readiness is a bare TCP probe of the fixed port - its own comment says so, 'the port answers, whoever opened it' - and nothing checks that this run's child is the process that bound it. On a Docker-free host with something already listening on E2E_NATS_PORT (14222 by default), the child fails to bind and exits, wait_for_nats succeeds against the foreign server, and the acceptance run proceeds against it: the listener's bus.ConnectOwningStream can reconcile that server's ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS stream and the run registers its fake session and publishes fixtures there. Found by the security pass; verified in the code by the reviewer. NOT BLOCKING, and the reasoning is recorded so the judgement is auditable rather than silent: the run fails loudly rather than passing falsely - stop_nats kills a dead pid, the foreign server stays up, and the bus-down step then answers something other than 503 and exits 1 - so no false green is produced; CI is unaffected, since CI has Docker and takes the container backend; the Go-test backend cannot hit this, since internal/testnats/local.go starts nats-server with -p -1 and reads the chosen port from the server's own log; and the whole fallback is explicitly temporary with an owner, dispatch://INFRA-250, which deletes it. The remedy if it is kept: refuse an occupied port before starting, and take readiness from the owned child rather than from the port, failing while the child is dead. Recorded in Not proven / risk and named to the architect for routing to INFRA-250.
